answer: One dune sand trap per identity is held by one anchor peg whose serial binds its key, with a 75-credit bond. After each gale the owner files pre- and post-storm mass; the delta is the sand gain. Auditors reweigh the trap, verify the anchor serial, and recompute the gain from the gale wind table, burning the bond over 5 percent deviation or serial reuse. The first filing costs 33, the k-th 33+6(k-1), so 1000 fakes pay 3,030,000 plus 75,000 locked bonds. A rented-trap ring fails: shared pegs and identical deltas expose reuse. An honest owner pays 33 once and recovers the bond after audit.
